title: BenchMeUp: Building Software Engineering Benchmarks from Natural-Language Specifications
title_zh: BenchMeUp：从自然语言规格说明构建软件工程基准

paragraphs.en: BenchMeUp从自然语言规格说明自动构建软件工程基准，大幅降低人工成本并支持端到端评估。 Software-engineering research relies on benchmarks that evaluate new techniques on a set of problem instances. Unfortunately, manually constructing benchmarks is labor-intensive, as researchers must find suitable instances, prepare execution environments, establish expected outcomes, and validate correctness. This paper presents BenchMeUp, an approach for automatically creating software-engineering benchmarks from natural-language specifications. Given a specification defining the desired instances, data sources, and evaluation procedures, BenchMeUp generates search rules and a construction plan, invokes parallel LLM agents that identify candidate instances and construct executable instances, validates the results in fresh execution environments, and packages the instances behind a unified command-line interface. We evaluate the approach on four tasks: program repair, issue reproduction, compiler autotuning, and fixing static-analysis warnings. Targeting 50 instances per task (200 in total), BenchMeUp constructs 198 instances, of which 196 (99\%) are successfully packaged. Search and construction take 36 minutes and \$0.79 per instance, on average. Evaluating eight existing techniques on the generated benchmarks, we find that 189 of 196 packaged instances (96\%) support end-to-end evaluation, allowing users to study the effectiveness of the techniques. Checking every constructed instance against its source, the specification, and its expected outcome, we find that 180 of 198 (91\%) meet all criteria, compared with 10 of 200 instances delivered by Codex (general-purpose coding agent). Overall, we show that LLM-based agents can automate benchmark construction across diverse software-engineering tasks and produce executable instances that existing techniques can use, while validity beyond execution still needs to be checked.
paragraphs.zh: BenchMeUp从自然语言规格说明自动构建软件工程基准，大幅降低人工成本并支持端到端评估。软件工程研究依赖于在一组问题实例上评估新技术的基准。 遗憾的是，人工构建基准非常耗费人力，因为研究人员必须寻找合适的实例、准备执行环境、确定预期结果并验证正确性。 本文提出BenchMeUp，一种从自然语言规格说明自动创建软件工程基准的方法。 给定一个定义了所需实例、数据来源和评估流程的规格说明，BenchMeUp会生成搜索规则和构建计划，调用并行的大语言模型智能体来识别候选实例并构建可执行实例，在全新的执行环境中验证结果，并通过统一的命令行界面打包这些实例。 我们在四项任务上评估该方法：程序修复、问题复现、编译器自动调优以及修复静态分析警告。 以每项任务50个实例（共200个）为目标，BenchMeUp构建了198个实例，其中196个（99%）被成功打包。 平均而言，每个实例的搜索和构建耗时36分钟、花费0.79美元。 通过在生成的基准上评估八种现有技术，我们发现196个已打包实例中有189个（96%）支持端到端评估，使用户能够研究这些技术的有效性。 将每个构建的实例与其来源、规格说明及预期结果逐一核对后，我们发现198个实例中有180个（91%）满足全部标准，而Codex（通用编码智能体）交付的200个实例中仅有10个达标。 总体而言，我们表明基于大语言模型的智能体能够跨多样的软件工程任务自动构建基准，并产出可供现有技术使用的可执行实例，但执行之外的效度仍有待检验。
